d6c2e1a113f9: How to add MultiDatePick to an App Page, Home Page, or Experience Site
371add5392e8: Build a config in the MultiDatePick Setup Wizard, then on a surface with no record context set two properties: Config Name and Static Parent Record Id, the record the dates attach to. The config supplies every other setting.
5d60bb4a1845: Create or pick a parent record
50d1364f3394: Create the parent record the dates will attach to, then copy its 15-18 character record Id.
6c4136072fb8: Drag MultiDatePick onto your App Page or Home Page in Lightning App Builder, or onto an Experience Site page in Experience Builder (Custom Components).
7f93f0c3081f: Paste the parent record Id into Static Parent Record Id, then fill in Child Object API Name, Date Field API Name and Relationship Field API Name (or set a Config Name from the Setup Wizard). The Save button appears once all four are set.
735472c45f4b: Assign the MultiDatePick - User permission set. On a public Experience Site, assign the MultiDatePick - Guest permission set to the guest user, add read and create on any objects of your own, a guest sharing rule, then activate the site.
c9e388dd2116: App Pages, Home Pages & Experience Sites
d77c3483e46e: MultiDatePick works on every Lightning surface, not just record pages. The trick is one property: <t1>Static Parent Record Id</t1>.
3b09297c899a: MultiDatePick saves the dates you pick as records on a related object, each one linked back to a <t1>parent record</t1>. The component just needs to know <t2>which</t2> parent.
877e90a86a92: <t1>On a record page</t1> (e.g. an Event record), Salesforce automatically hands the component the current record's Id (the <t2>recordId</t2>). Nothing extra to configure.
6131253f4ac7: <t1>On an App Page, Home Page, or Experience Site</t1>, there is no "current record." Salesforce passes nothing. With no parent, the component has nowhere to save, so it <t2>hides the Save button by design</t2> rather than show one that fails on click.
bf994d15d255: <t1>The fix is the Static Parent Record Id property.</t1> Paste a specific parent record's Id into it, and the component behaves exactly as if it were sitting on that record's page. It is a property you set in the builder. It has nothing to do with a Salesforce Static Resource, which is a separate feature for uploaded files.
eb7a70fe8d8e: <t1>Find <t2>Static Parent Record Id</t2> in the property panel after you drag MultiDatePick onto an App Page or Home Page in Lightning App Builder, or onto a page in Experience Builder.</t1>
6013a32c9e44: Static Parent Record Id vs. a Flow: when to use which
f2f20608ee13: Static Parent Record Id points the component at <t1>one fixed parent</t1>, so <t2>every visitor sees the same record.</t2> That is perfect for some cases and wrong for others. When the record needs to change per user or per visit, drive it from a <t3>Screen Flow</t3> instead. Drop the component on a Flow screen and bind its <t4>Parent Record Id</t4> to a variable the Flow resolves at runtime.
c6255d4cb1c4: Use Static Parent Record Id when the record is the same for everybody
31ac12f97461: <t1>A public booking page:</t1> a guest-facing "request an appointment" page where every booking attaches to the same parent record (one office, location, or resource). A fixed Id is exactly right.
ad8fb1506b4c: <t1>One org-wide calendar:</t1> a single "Company Closures" record, or one shared resource everyone books, that never changes per user.
85f3004adfd2: <t1>A fixed dashboard anchor</t1> on an App or Home page that always points at the same master record.
0c2e39d43455: <t1>Rule of thumb: reach for Static Parent Record Id when the answer to "whose record is this?" is "the same one for everybody."</t1>
c70cbaf9902d: Use a Flow when the record is chosen at runtime
ec76286d9d25: <t1>Per-user records:</t1> each person sees only their own (for example, every contractor lands on their own PTO calendar). The Flow does a <t2>Get Records</t2> where the owner or a linked Contact = <t3>{!$User.Id}</t3>, stores the Id, and passes it to the component.
59d06fcceb4e: <t1>URL-driven:</t1> a Flow input variable reads <t2>?id=…</t2> from the link, so one page serves many records. This works for guests too, with no login.
f540261be7b6: <t1>Pick-first:</t1> screen 1 lets the user search or choose (an employee, a room, a client); screen 2 shows that record's calendar.
3c5a7d222c2c: <t1>Guest sites:</t1> on a no-login public site the "user" is a single shared guest, so per-user (<t2>$User</t2>) resolution does not apply. Either share one record through Static Parent Record Id, or drive it from a URL parameter through a Flow. True per-user calendars need logged-in users.
26651f89a554: Copy the config name in the Setup Wizard, paste it with the parent record Id, and the calendar is ready. The config supplies every other setting.

79ccbd60124d: Public guest sites: the five-step checklist
c74ca7ff6455: A public Experience Cloud page lets anyone book without logging in. Do all five before you test as a guest. Steps 4 and 5 are the two most often missed. See it working on the <t1>live demo</t1>, a public guest site.
ad18f8e13471: Give the site guest user Read, and Create if guests submit, on each object the component uses. Guests can never Edit or Delete. That is a Salesforce guest license rule for every app, so keep edit and cancel on pages behind a login.
88417118f4c0: Read on every field the calendar shows. Edit on every field it writes, including status, time and relationship fields. Include the resource business hours and closure fields too.
0bddfcf0a07f: A Read sharing rule for the guest user, so guests can see the records. The object's external org-wide default must be Private for the rule to apply. A rule deployed as metadata needs one click on <t1>Recalculate</t1> in Sharing Settings.
312c9589064e: Assign <t1>MultiDatePick - Guest</t1> to the site's guest user. It carries the Apex class access the calendar loads its data through, plus the read and create rights a guest may have on the MultiDatePick objects.
163fa42c0cd6: Publishing and activating are separate steps. Guests only see an activated site.
1035a9539e2e: Two org settings guests also need
851e27a03634: Guests cannot own records, so Salesforce assigns every guest booking to a default owner. Set it in Experience Workspaces, Administration, Preferences.
58a75191a21f: A booking that points at a resource or parent needs guest Read on that record, or the save fails with a cross-reference error. Use a custom object for anything guests book against: guest access to Contacts and Accounts is heavily restricted.
8e145daa01d6: Planning a public booking page? <t1>Self-service booking on a Salesforce Experience Cloud site</t1> covers what guests can do and which view to show them.
